q: (Abdullaah bin Ummi Maktoom once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ while Rasulullaah ﷺ was preaching Islaam to a few leaders of the Quraysh. Because he was blind, he did not realise that Rasulullaah ﷺ was occupied with the others and he kept insisting that Rasulullaah ﷺ should teach him something. Since his arrival disturbed the discussion and acceding to his request would interrupt what was being said to the Mushrikeen leaders, Rasulullaah ﷺ ignored him, thinking that he would speak to him later on. Since the opportunity to address the Quraysh leaders was so rare if any of them accepted Islaam, it would influence many others to follow. Rasulullaah EYE's reaction became evident on his face when he frowned. Referring to this, Allaah says,)
v.s: He [i.e., the Prophet (ﷺ) ] frowned and turned away
v.c: He frowned and turned ˹his attention˺ away,

q: ...because a blind man came to him
v.s: Because there came to him the blind man, [interrupting].
v.c: ˹simply˺ because the blind man came to him ˹interrupting˺.

q: How do you know that perhaps he
v.s: But what would make you perceive, [O Muhammad], that perhaps he might be purified
v.c: You never know ˹O Prophet˺, perhaps he may be purified,

q: ...or he may take heed and the advice will prove beneficial
v.s: Or be reminded and the remembrance would benefit him?
v.c: or he may be mindful, benefitting from the reminder.

v.s: As for he who thinks himself without need,
v.c: As for the one who was indifferent,

q: (instead of attending to the blind sincere Muslim)...
v.s: To him you give attention.
v.c: you gave him your ˹undivided˺ attention,

q: ...when there would be no blame on you if he is not purified
(because they were not Muslims in the first place).
v.s: And not upon you [is any blame] if he will not be purified.
v.c: even though you are not to blame if he would not be purified.

v.s: But as for he who came to you striving [for knowledge]
v.c: But as for the one who came to you, eager ˹to learn˺,

v.s: While he fears [God],
v.c: being in awe ˹of Allah˺,

v.s: From him you are distracted.
v.c: you were inattentive to him.

q: This should never be. Indeed this
v.s: No! Indeed, they [i.e., these verses] are a reminder;
v.c: But no! This ˹revelation˺ is truly a reminder.

v.s: So whoever wills may remember it.
v.c: So let whoever wills be mindful of it.

v.s: [It is recorded] in honoured sheets,
v.c: It is ˹written˺ on pages held in honour—

q: (from errors and beyond the reach of the impure Shayaateen)...
v.s: Exalted and purified,
v.c: highly esteemed, purified—

q: (the angels and the Sahabah ﵃) who were the scribes)...
v.s: [Carried] by the hands of messenger-angels,
v.c: by the hands of angel-scribes,

q: (The “scribes” mentioned here can also refer to those) Sahabah ﵊ who used to reward in writing the Qur'aan during the lifetime of Rasulullaah ﷺ.)
v.s: Noble and dutiful.
v.c: honourable and virtuous.

q: (Despite all the favours Allaah has blessed him with, the Kaafir chooses to worship others instead.)
v.s: Destroyed [i.e., cursed] is man; how disbelieving is he.
v.c: Condemned are ˹disbelieving˺ humans! How ungrateful they are ˹to Allah˺!

q: From what did Allaah create him?
v.s: From what thing [i.e., substance] did He create him?
v.c: From what substance did He create them?

q: From a drop of semen Allaah created him, made him in due proportion
(with all the parts of his body in proportion to each other)...
v.s: From a sperm-drop He created him and destined for him;
v.c: He created them from a sperm-drop, and ordained their development.

q: ...and then eased the way for him
(to come into this world and to survive in it. By sending the Ambiyaa ﵊ and the Divine Scriptures, Allaah also made it easy for man to understand right and wrong).
v.s: Then He eased the way for him;
v.c: Then He makes the way easy for them,

m: and provides a grave for him
q: Allaah then gave him death and concealed him in a grave.
v.s: Then He causes his death and provides a grave for him.
v.c: then causes them to die and be buried.

q: Then Allaah shall resurrect him when He wills.
v.s: Then when He wills, He will resurrect him.
v.c: Then when He wills, He will resurrect them.

v.s: No! He [i.e., man] has not yet accomplished what He commanded him.
v.c: But no! They have failed to comply with what He ordered.

q: Let man look at his food
(for) in it he will recognise the power of Allaah and realise Allaah's tremendous favours to him).
v.s: Then let mankind look at his food -
v.c: Let people then consider their food:

q: We make the rain pour forth in abundance. (The rain nourishes the soil and causes seeds to germinate and sprout.])
v.s: How We poured down water in torrents,
v.c: how We pour down rain in abundance

q: (when the shoots of the seeds start to pierce through the ground,)
We cause the earth to part into clefts
(split to allow the shoots to reach the surface and grow).
v.s: Then We broke open the earth, splitting [it with sprouts],
v.c: and meticulously split the earth open ˹for sprouts˺,

q: We then grow on the earth grains
v.s: And caused to grow within it grain
v.c: causing grain to grow in it,

v.s: And grapes and herbage
v.c: as well as grapes and greens,

v.s: And olive and palm trees
v.c: and olives and palm trees,

v.s: And gardens of dense shrubbery
v.c: and dense orchards,

v.s: And fruit and grass -
v.c: and fruit and fodder—

q: and for the benefit of your animals.
v.s: [As] enjoyment [i.e., provision] for you and your grazing livestock.
v.c: all as ˹a means of˺ sustenance for you and your animals.

v.s: But when there comes the Deafening Blast
v.c: Then, when the Deafening Blast comes to pass—

q: ...on that day man will run from his brother...
v.s: On the Day a man will flee from his brother
v.c: on that Day every person will flee from their own siblings,

v.s: And his mother and his father
v.c: and ˹even˺ their mother and father,

q: (No one will want to help another because everyone will be concerned only about trying to save themselves.)
v.s: And his wife and his children,
v.c: and ˹even˺ their spouse and children.

q: On that day every one of them will be preoccupied with a predicament
that will make him oblivious of
v.s: For every man, that Day, will be a matter adequate for him.
v.c: For then everyone will have enough concern of their own.

q: On that day many faces shall be radiant
v.s: [Some] faces, that Day, will be bright -
v.c: On that Day ˹some˺ faces will be bright,

q: (These will be the Mu'mineen destined for Jannah.)
v.s: Laughing, rejoicing at good news.
v.c: laughing and rejoicing,

v.s: And [other] faces, that Day, will have upon them dust.
v.c: while ˹other˺ faces will be dusty,

v.s: Blackness will cover them.
v.c: cast in gloom—

q: These will be the sinful Kuffaar.
v.s: Those are the disbelievers, the wicked ones.
v.c: those are the disbelievers, the ˹wicked˺ sinners.
